date_note: The page gives only its own publication day (23 November); it says users were notified that day.
title: European Commission says cyberattack disrupted EU Academy platform and leaked user data
summary: An agency report carried by Shorouk News says the European Commission announced its EU Academy platform was disrupted by a cyberattack that leaked registered users' personal data. Spokesperson Thomas Regnier said users were notified on the Academy website. Voria.gr and Mikrometoxos.gr report public access was disabled. Euronews (French edition) reports, citing two sources familiar with the matter, that the Commission suspects a China-backed actor; it says the breach is not fully contained.
plain: The European Commission says an attack disrupted its EU Academy learning platform and leaked registered users' personal data, according to agency and Greek reports.
exec: The Commission says user data from an EU platform leaked; the report ties it to an earlier campaign against Commission systems.
action: As the Commission's spokesperson says, users were notified through the EU Academy website; check that notice. General advice: be alert to phishing that uses your registration details.

validation.note: Shorouk News, Voria.gr and Mikrometoxos.gr each relay the Commission spokesperson's statement that EU Academy was hit; the Commission's own page could not be loaded.
